hints: You want every post connected with the least total wire, and you never need a loop (a loop always has one wire you could drop). What kind of structure is 'connect everything with no loops at minimum cost'?

A minimum spanning tree on the complete graph of posts. Because every pair is an edge, Prim's algorithm with an array (no heap) is simplest: keep best[i] = cheapest wire from post i to the tree built so far.

1. Set best[0] = 0, all others to infinity.
  2. Repeat n times: pick the post not in the tree with the smallest best.
  3. Add it to the tree and add best to the total.
  4. Update best[j] for every other post with its Manhattan distance to the new post.
  5. Return the total.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Kruskal: list all n² pairs, sort them, and add with union-find.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Array-based Prim's on the dense graph: n rounds, each scanning n posts.

explain: For the 5 sample posts, Prim's starts at (0,0). It adds (2,2) at cost 4, then (5,2) at cost 3 from (2,2), then (7,0) at cost 4 from (5,2), and finally (3,10) at cost 9 from (2,2). The total is 4+3+4+9 = 20. A single post needs no wire, so the answer is 0.
recognize: Connect all points with minimum total cost → minimum spanning tree (Prim's for a dense/complete graph).
